pack.name: Global baseline (standards and frameworks, not law)
pack.scope: Controls drawn from voluntary standards and frameworks that customers, auditors and procurement teams ask for everywhere: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, NIST CSF 2.0, NIST AI RMF 1.0, OWASP ASVS, WCAG 2.2 AA, SBOM and open-source licence hygiene. These are NOT statutes. Nothing in this pack creates a legal obligation by itself; obligations arise when a contract, a certification scheme or a law incorporates one of these standards by reference. This pack deliberately excludes: national law of any kind, sector regulation, export controls, employment law, tax and corporate law.

sources.note: Host blocks automated requests (HTTP 403 on check); URL is the canonical entry point and was not machine-verified. The standard itself is paywalled.

pack.verificationRequired: Automated technical assessment. Not legal advice. Standards are revised and clause numbering changes between editions (ISO/IEC 27001:2013 to :2022 renumbered Annex A entirely; OWASP ASVS 5.0 renumbered chapters relative to 4.0.x). lastReviewed is null: no control in this pack has been confirmed against the current official text. Confirm every control against the edition your organisation is actually certified or contracted against, and have a qualified professional confirm anything consequential.

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.1 (Policies for information security)
controls.requirement: An information security policy set is defined, approved by management, published, communicated to relevant personnel and reviewed at planned intervals.
evidenceHints: doc: SECURITY.md, docs/security/policy.md, an ISMS policy register
doc: evidence of management approval and a review date
ask: who owns the policy set and when was it last reviewed

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.15 (Access control)
controls.requirement: Rules for physical and logical access to information and other associated assets are established and implemented on the basis of business and information security requirements.
evidenceHints: code: authorisation middleware, policy files, role/permission definitions
config: IAM policies, RBAC manifests, database grants
cmd: list of accounts with administrative privileges

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.19 (Information security in supplier relationships)
controls.requirement: Processes and procedures manage the information security risks associated with the use of supplier products and services.
evidenceHints: doc: vendor register, subprocessor list, signed DPAs
config: third-party services referenced in infrastructure and application configuration
ask: is there a supplier onboarding security review

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.23 (Information security for use of cloud services)
controls.requirement: Processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services are established in accordance with the organisation's information security requirements.
evidenceHints: config: cloud provider account structure, region configuration, IaC definitions
doc: an exit or portability plan naming the data export path
ask: which cloud regions actually hold production data

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.24 and A 5.26 (Incident management planning, preparation and response)
controls.requirement: Incident management responsibilities and procedures are planned and prepared, and information security incidents are responded to in accordance with documented procedures.
evidenceHints: doc: incident response runbook with named roles and escalation path
doc: evidence the plan has been exercised at least once
code: alerting rules and on-call routing configuration

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.30 (ICT readiness for business continuity)
controls.requirement: ICT readiness is planned, implemented, maintained and tested against business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
evidenceHints: config: backup schedule, retention and replication configuration
cmd: date and outcome of the most recent restore test
doc: stated RTO and RPO per service

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.34 (Privacy and protection of PII)
controls.requirement: Requirements for the preservation of privacy and protection of personally identifiable information are identified and met according to applicable legislation, regulation and contractual requirements.
evidenceHints: doc: data inventory or record of processing
code: models and schemas that carry personal data fields
ask: which national privacy laws the organisation considers applicable

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 6.3 (Information security awareness, education and training)
controls.requirement: Personnel and relevant interested parties receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates relevant to their job function.
evidenceHints: doc: training records with dates and completion status
ask: do engineers receive secure development training distinct from generic awareness training

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.8 (Management of technical vulnerabilities)
controls.requirement: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use is obtained, exposure evaluated and appropriate measures taken.
evidenceHints: config: dependency scanning in CI (Dependabot, Renovate, osv-scanner, Trivy)
cmd: current count of unremediated high/critical advisories
doc: a remediation SLA per severity

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.10 (Information deletion)
controls.requirement: Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media is deleted when no longer required.
evidenceHints: code: a scheduled job, TTL or lifecycle rule that actually deletes records
config: object storage lifecycle policies, log retention settings, backup expiry
ask: does deletion propagate to backups, search indexes, caches and analytics

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.12 (Data leakage prevention)
controls.requirement: Data leakage prevention measures are applied to systems, networks and other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.
evidenceHints: config: secret scanning in CI and in the repository history
code: log redaction or masking helpers applied at the logging boundary
cmd: grep of production logs for token, password, email or identifier patterns

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.15 and A 8.16 (Logging and monitoring activities)
controls.requirement: Logs recording activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events are produced, stored, protected and analysed, and networks, systems and applications are monitored for anomalous behaviour.
evidenceHints: code: audit log emission on authentication, authorisation and data access events
config: log retention period and access restrictions on the log store
ask: can you reconstruct who accessed a given record and when

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.24 (Use of cryptography)
controls.requirement: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, are defined and implemented.
evidenceHints: code: cipher suites, algorithms and key sizes used in the codebase
config: TLS configuration, at-rest encryption settings, KMS or vault integration
cmd: search for hand-rolled cryptography or deprecated primitives (MD5, SHA-1, ECB, static IVs)

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.25, A 8.26 and A 8.28 (Secure development life cycle, application security requirements, secure coding)
controls.requirement: Rules for secure development are established and applied, security requirements are specified for applications, and secure coding principles are applied to software development.
evidenceHints: config: SAST, linting and security rules enforced in CI as a blocking gate
doc: a security review step in the pull request template or contribution guide
code: presence of a threat model or abuse-case documentation

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.31 and A 8.32 (Separation of environments, change management)
controls.requirement: Development, test and production environments are separated and secured, and changes to information processing facilities and systems are subject to change management procedures.
evidenceHints: config: separate credentials and accounts per environment, no shared production secrets
cmd: check whether production data is copied into non-production environments
config: branch protection and required review before deployment

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27701 (Privacy Information Management System)
controls.requirement: The organisation determines and documents its role for each processing activity (PII controller, PII processor, or both) and applies the corresponding set of PIMS controls.
evidenceHints: doc: a statement of role per processing activity
doc: customer-facing contracts that assign controller/processor roles
ask: are there activities where the organisation is a controller over its own customers' end users

controls.instrument: ISO/IEC 27701 (PIMS) — collection limitation and data minimisation
controls.requirement: Collection of personally identifiable information is limited to what is relevant, proportional and necessary for the identified purposes, and purposes are documented before collection.
evidenceHints: code: request/response DTOs and form fields, checked field by field against a stated purpose
code: analytics and telemetry payloads, which are the usual source of over-collection
ask: which fields could be removed without breaking a stated purpose

controls.instrument: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria — Common Criteria (control environment, risk assessment, monitoring)
controls.requirement: The entity demonstrates a defined control environment with assigned responsibilities, performs risk assessment covering fraud and change, and monitors the operation of its controls.
evidenceHints: doc: org chart or responsibility matrix for security controls
doc: a risk register with owners and review dates
ask: has a SOC 2 Type I or Type II report ever been issued, and for which criteria

controls.instrument: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria — logical and physical access controls
controls.requirement: Access to systems and data is authorised, provisioned, modified and removed based on role, and access is reviewed periodically. Removal on termination is timely.
evidenceHints: cmd: current list of users with production access and their last access review date
doc: joiner/mover/leaver procedure with a target removal window
config: MFA enforcement on identity provider and cloud console

controls.instrument: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria — Availability
controls.requirement: Capacity is monitored against objectives, environmental and recovery infrastructure is maintained, and recovery procedures are tested. Only claim this category if it is in the audit scope.
evidenceHints: config: monitoring and alerting on saturation signals
doc: published or contractual availability commitment
cmd: most recent disaster recovery exercise report

controls.instrument: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — GOVERN function
controls.requirement: Cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations and policy are established, communicated and monitored, including roles, responsibilities, authorities and supply chain risk management.
evidenceHints: doc: a named accountable owner for cybersecurity risk
doc: supply chain risk management practice covering third-party software
ask: how are cybersecurity risks escalated to leadership

controls.instrument: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 — DETECT, RESPOND and RECOVER functions
controls.requirement: Anomalies and adverse events are detected and analysed, response actions are executed and communicated, and assets and operations are restored according to a plan.
evidenceHints: config: detection rules mapped to plausible attack paths, not just infrastructure health checks
doc: communications plan naming who tells customers and regulators
cmd: mean time to detect and mean time to recover from the last incidents

controls.instrument: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — GOVERN function
controls.requirement: Policies, processes, roles and accountability structures for AI risk are in place, including named ownership of each AI system and a process for retiring or disabling it.
evidenceHints: doc: an AI system inventory with an owner per system
doc: an AI use policy covering acceptable and prohibited uses
ask: who can switch an AI feature off, and how fast

controls.instrument: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — MAP function
controls.requirement: Context is established: intended purpose, deployment setting, affected individuals and groups, capabilities and limitations, and foreseeable misuse of each AI system.
evidenceHints: doc: a system card or model card stating intended and out-of-scope uses
code: prompt templates and system instructions, which encode the actual intended behaviour
ask: which decisions about people does this system influence

controls.instrument: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — MEASURE function
controls.requirement: AI risks are analysed, benchmarked and tracked with appropriate metrics and methods, including evaluation of validity, reliability, safety, bias and robustness, with results recorded.
evidenceHints: code: an evaluation suite in the repository with a stored baseline and thresholds
cmd: date and result of the last evaluation run against the deployed model version
doc: bias or fairness testing where the system affects people

controls.instrument: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — MANAGE function
controls.requirement: Identified AI risks are prioritised, treated, monitored in production, and responded to, including incident handling and mechanisms to recover from AI system failures.
evidenceHints: config: production monitoring of AI outputs (refusal rate, drift, complaint volume)
doc: an AI incident procedure distinct from the generic security incident procedure
code: a kill switch, feature flag or fallback path when the model is unavailable or misbehaving

controls.instrument: OWASP ASVS — authentication and session management chapters
controls.requirement: Authentication verifies credentials securely, protects against credential stuffing and brute force, and sessions are generated, transmitted, rotated and terminated safely.
evidenceHints: code: password hashing algorithm and parameters, session cookie flags, token lifetimes
code: logout and session invalidation paths, including on password change
config: rate limiting on authentication endpoints

controls.instrument: OWASP ASVS — access control chapter
controls.requirement: Access control decisions are enforced server-side on every request, deny by default, and object-level authorisation prevents users from reaching records belonging to others.
evidenceHints: code: every route handler that accepts an id parameter — check for an ownership or tenancy predicate
code: multi-tenant queries, checking the tenant filter is not optional
cmd: tests that assert a 403/404 for a foreign resource id

controls.instrument: OWASP ASVS — validation, sanitisation and encoding chapter
controls.requirement: Untrusted input is validated at the trust boundary with positive (allow-list) schemas, and output is encoded for its destination context to prevent injection.
evidenceHints: code: schema validation at controller/handler entry points
code: string-concatenated SQL, shell commands or template rendering
config: Content-Security-Policy header for browser surfaces

controls.instrument: OWASP ASVS — configuration and secret management chapters
controls.requirement: Secrets are not embedded in source code or images, configuration is hardened for production, and dependencies are inventoried and kept current.
evidenceHints: cmd: secret scan across the working tree and git history
config: how secrets reach the runtime (environment, vault, mounted file)
config: debug flags, stack traces and verbose errors disabled in production

controls.instrument: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
controls.requirement: Non-text content has text alternatives, structure and relationships are programmatically determinable, and text and interface component contrast meet the AA thresholds.
evidenceHints: code: img/icon components without alt text or accessible names
code: headings, lists, tables and landmarks used semantically rather than visually
cmd: automated contrast audit output, plus the manual checks automation cannot perform

controls.instrument: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — SC 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
controls.requirement: All functionality is operable by keyboard without traps, the keyboard focus indicator is visible, and the focused component is not entirely hidden by author-created content.
evidenceHints: code: click handlers on non-interactive elements, custom widgets without key handling
code: sticky headers, cookie banners and toasts that can cover the focused element
cmd: keyboard-only walkthrough of the primary user journey, recorded

controls.instrument: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
controls.requirement: Dragging has a single-pointer alternative, pointer targets meet the minimum size, previously entered information is not required to be re-entered, and authentication does not depend on a cognitive function test without an alternative.
evidenceHints: code: drag-and-drop interactions, sliders and reorderable lists
code: login flows using puzzles or transcription, and whether paste is blocked on password fields
code: multi-step forms that re-ask for data already supplied

controls.instrument: WCAG 2.2 Level AA — SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and SC 4.1.3 Status Messages
controls.requirement: Custom interface components expose a correct name, role and state to assistive technology, and status messages are announced without receiving focus.
evidenceHints: code: custom dropdowns, modals, tabs and toggles and their ARIA attributes
code: live regions for async results, validation summaries and toasts
cmd: screen reader pass on the primary journey (note: SC 4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete in WCAG 2.2)

controls.instrument: SBOM formats: SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962:2021) and CycloneDX
controls.requirement: A software bill of materials is generated automatically as part of the build for each released artefact, in a machine-readable standard format, and includes component name, version, supplier and licence.
evidenceHints: config: an SBOM generation step in the CI pipeline
cmd: syft, cdxgen, or the native SBOM output of the package manager
doc: where SBOMs are stored and for how long

controls.instrument: SBOM retention and disclosure practice
controls.requirement: SBOMs are retained per released version and are retrievable for the supported life of that version, so that a newly disclosed vulnerability can be traced to affected releases.
evidenceHints: cmd: retrieve the SBOM for the oldest still-supported release
doc: a stated support window per release
ask: could you answer 'which of our releases contain library X version Y' within a day

controls.instrument: Open-source licence hygiene — declared project licence and SPDX identifiers
controls.requirement: The project declares its own licence unambiguously in a LICENSE file and in package metadata, using a valid SPDX identifier, consistent across every distribution channel.
evidenceHints: doc: LICENSE or LICENSE.txt at the repository root
config: the licence field in package.json, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, Cargo.toml, go.mod metadata
cmd: check that the declared identifier matches the actual licence text

controls.instrument: Open-source licence hygiene — third-party inventory, attribution and NOTICE
controls.requirement: A current inventory of third-party components and their licences exists, attribution and licence text required by those licences is reproduced in the distributed artefact, and unknown or missing licences are treated as blocking.
evidenceHints: cmd: dependency licence report from the package manager or an SBOM query
doc: NOTICE file or a third-party licences screen in the product
cmd: count of dependencies with licence 'UNKNOWN', 'NOASSERTION' or empty

controls.instrument: Contributor IP provenance — CLA or DCO
controls.requirement: Inbound contributions are covered by a clear IP mechanism (a contributor licence agreement or a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off), and the mechanism is actually enforced rather than merely documented.
evidenceHints: doc: CONTRIBUTING.md stating CLA or DCO
config: a CI check enforcing sign-off or CLA acceptance on pull requests
cmd: sample recent merged commits for the enforcement signal

controls.instrument: Build provenance and artefact integrity (SLSA-style provenance, signed releases)
controls.requirement: Released artefacts are built from an identified source revision by an auditable build process, and are signed or accompanied by verifiable provenance so consumers can detect substitution.
evidenceHints: config: release pipeline definition, including whether builds are reproducible from a tagged commit
cmd: verify the signature or attestation on the latest published artefact
ask: can a consumer verify the artefact without trusting the download channel
